housing.summary: Mumbai is India's most expensive rental market. Expats typically rent furnished flats in areas like Bandra, Powai, Lower Parel, and Worli. Leases usually run 11 months (to avoid stamp-duty rules on 12-month registration) and often require brokerage of one month's rent plus stamp duty and registration on the leave-and-license agreement. Landlords frequently prefer company leases for corporate tenants.

banking.summary: Foreign nationals resident in India can open resident savings accounts; non-residents use NRE/NRO accounts. Major banks include HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Axis, and Kotak Mahindra, plus international banks like HSBC, Citi, and Standard Chartered. Account opening requires KYC documentation and is generally straightforward once a PAN and local address proof are available.
required_docs: Proof of local address (leave-and-license agreement/utility bill)
FRRO registration / employment proof where applicable

schools.summary: Mumbai has a wide range of international and private schools serving expat families, concentrated in South Mumbai, Bandra, Powai, and the western suburbs. Admissions are competitive and often require early application; fees at international schools are among the highest in India.

legal_admin.summary: Foreign nationals on long-stay visas (employment, student, etc.) valid for more than 180 days must register with the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Mumbai, typically within 14 days of arrival, via the e-FRRO online portal. Registration produces a residential permit and is required for many downstream services.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with the FRRO Mumbai via the e-FRRO portal within 14 days of arrival (for visas exceeding 180 days); obtain residential permit / registration certificate.

tax_finance.summary: India taxes residents on worldwide income; tax residency is determined by days of physical presence (generally 182 days or more in a financial year, with additional tests). A Permanent Account Number (PAN) is mandatory for salary, banking, and property transactions. The financial year runs April to March, and returns are typically due by 31 July for individuals.

transport.summary: Mumbai's public transport is dominated by the suburban railway network ('local trains'), supplemented by BEST buses, an expanding Metro network, monorail, black-and-yellow taxis, autorickshaws (in the suburbs), and app-based cabs. Suburban trains are the backbone of daily commuting.
transport.network_name: Mumbai Suburban Railway / BEST buses / Mumbai Metro
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Foreign nationals can drive on an International Driving Permit for a limited period; longer-term residents should obtain an Indian driving licence through the Regional Transport Office (RTO), which may allow conversion of a valid foreign licence for residents.
transport.healthcare_registration: No universal public-health registration for expats; most rely on private health insurance and private hospitals (e.g. Lilavati, Kokilaben, Hinduja). Employer group insurance is common. Public hospitals exist but are heavily used.
